notes.decision: Untranslated word-fragment qualifying the presbyter; possibly the start of a Greek-derived adjective (ἐπάνω, ἐπανήκω) or a hapax title. Cf. line 25's lost word ending in -ⲙⲟⲥ which may be a parallel Greek loanword.
Compound ⲣⲉϥ-ϣⲙϣⲉ ('one who serves') + ⲉⲓⲇⲱⲗⲟⲛ (Greek εἴδωλον 'idol'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' The presbyter is a 'doer of idol-service' = pagan priest.

Distinguished from accumulated ⲡⲇⲟⲣⲙⲁ 'people/community' (= δῆμος): here ⲡⲇⲟⲅⲙⲁ = Greek δόγμα 'doctrine, teaching' (already in glossary as ⲁⲟⲅⲙⲁ). The chapter title and the presbyter's question both concern why this doctrine bears the name 'doctrine of Sin.'

Translated 'pluck/gather' from agricultural context (grape harvest, line 33 ⲛⲁⲭⲁⲗⲉϩ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲃⲱ ⲛ̄ⲉⲗⲁⲗⲉ 'shall pluck on the grape-vine'). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ϫⲱⲗⲕ̄/ⲕⲱⲗⲉϫ 'pluck, gather (fruit).' Reduplicated form ⲭⲉⲗⲗⲉϩ may be intensive.

Doubled discourse-marker 'in this manner; this manner also,' parallel to glossary entry ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ ⲁⲛ 'in this same manner again.' Signals typological parallelism between the bitter-tree case and the grape-vine case in the presbyter's argument.

Tentatively rendered 'garden' based on possible Lyc reflex of Coptic ϭⲙⲡⲏ 'park, garden' (Crum 824). The agricultural imagery dominating this kephalaion (tree, fruit, planting/uprooting) supports a horticultural interpretation. Alternative readings include a proper name (disciple's name introducing the dialogue) or an abbreviated technical term. Confidence: low.
Analyzed as ⲙ̄-ⲡⲟⲩ-ⲙⲏⲛ + ⲟⲛ 'their not abiding again' (negative perfect of ⲙⲏⲛ 'remain, abide' + ⲟⲛ 'again'). Alternative: Greek-derived form. Translation tentative.

Analyzed as ⲉⲕ-ⲟ ⲛ̄-ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'you are in the likeness of' rather than ⲉⲕ-ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'you bring/bear,' since the parallel construction with ⲁⲩϣⲏⲛ 'a tree' is comparative. Per terminology guide, ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ rendered consistently as 'likeness.'

Verb meaning 'to set, place' (cf. line 8 ⲁⲩⲭⲁⲗⲉⲕ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'they set you in the cosmos'; line 12 ⲭⲁⲗⲉⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'remove out of the cosmos'; line 14 qualitative ⲭⲁⲗⲝ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'set in the cosmos'). Likely Lyc reflex of ϫⲁⲗⲟ/ϭⲁⲗⲟ 'set, lay, plant.' With ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'remove forth, take out.' Distinct from ⲭⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'draw' in glossary.
Discourse particle 'indeed, surely' (= Sah ϩⲁⲗⲱⲥ?). Recurs lines 9, 11. Translated 'indeed' consistently.

Substantive of unclear identity, functioning as the unspecified name by which the fruit is NOT called while still on the tree (parallel to ⲡϣⲏⲣⲉ ⲛⲧⲛⲟⲃⲉ 'son of sin' for the disciple). Possibly a positive epithet ('the ripe one,' 'the come-of-age') withheld until the fruit reaches maturity. Left transliterated due to uncertainty.
ⲧⲍⲉ = Lyc ⲛ̄ⲧϩⲉ 'in the manner of' (cf. ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲉ in glossary). Rendered 'in the manner of a fruit' to preserve the explicit comparative force.

Tentatively interpreted as Lyc 'his face' (variant of ⲛⲉϥϩⲟ; cf. ⲡⲍⲟ 'face' in glossary with ⲍ for ϩ, here ⲭ). The verb ⲃⲓ 'lift, carry' would govern this as 'he lifted his face upward to his disciples' — a narrative gesture introducing a new teaching. Alternative readings (e.g., 'his voice') possible.

Following accumulated vocabulary's tentative reading 'twelve,' though the form could plausibly represent 'thirty-two' (ⲙⲁⲁⲃ ⲥⲛⲟⲟⲩⲥ '30+2').
